record.paper_title: Advances in periodic difference equations with open problems
record.original_question: Let [f0, …, f_{p-1}] be a p-periodic system of continuous interval maps. For an integer k with 1 ≤ k ≤ p, form a folded system by composing blocks of k consecutive maps cyclically, producing maps F0, F1, … and hence a shorter-period system [F0, F1, …]. Determine the relationship between the set of least periods Per([f0, …, f_{p-1}]) of the original system and the set of least periods of the folded system.

evidence.quote: In general, for any 1 ≤ k ≤ p − 1, we can fold the maps fk−1 ◦ · · · ◦ f0 =: F0, f2k−1 ◦ · · · ◦ fk =: F1, f3k−1 ◦ · · · ◦ f2k =: F2, · · · to form another periodic system [F0, F1, ..., F p/gcd(p,k)].

Open Problem 3.1. Consider the p-periodic system [f0, ..., fp−1], and let 1 ≤ k ≤ p. Consider the maps F0, F1, . . . , F p/gcd(p,k) as defined in (3.1). What is the relationship between Per([f0, ..., fp−1]) and Per([F0, F1, ..., F p/gcd(p,k)])?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be an interval and let $f_0, f_1, \ldots, f_{p-1}: I \to I$ be continuous maps. Consider the non-autonomous (periodic) difference equation
$$x_{n+1} = f_{n \bmod p}(x_n), \qquad n \ge 0,$$
and call $[f_0, f_1, \ldots, f_{p-1}]$ the associated $p$-periodic system. A point $x \in I$ is said to be a periodic point of least period $m$ of this system if the sequence $\{x_n\}$ starting at $x_0 = x$ satisfies $x_{n+m} = x_n$ for all $n \ge 0$ with $m$ minimal. Define
$$\mathrm{Per}([f_0, \ldots, f_{p-1}]) := \{m \in \mathbb{N} : \text{the system has a periodic point of least period } m\}.$$

Fix an integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le p$, and define the folded maps
$$F_j := f_{(j+1)k - 1} \circ f_{(j+1)k - 2} \circ \cdots \circ f_{jk} \pmod{p}, \qquad j = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$$
Then $[F_0, F_1, \ldots, F_{q-1}]$ is a $q$-periodic system with $q = p/\gcd(p,k)$.

Determine the precise relationship between $\mathrm{Per}([f_0, \ldots, f_{p-1}])$ and $\mathrm{Per}([F_0, F_1, \ldots, F_{q-1}])$.
artifact.status_search_result: The folding/unfolding framework for periodic difference equations was introduced by Al-Salman and AlSharawi, and determining the exact relationship between the set of least periods of a periodic system and that of its folded counterpart remains an active research question. Partial results exist (e.g., when k divides p, or under Sharkovsky-type orderings), but a complete characterization in general does not appear to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Folding and unfolding in periodic difference equations
status_evidence.snippet: The notion of folding and unfolding... main goal is to obtain information on the periods of the subsequences obtained by folding the initial system.
status_evidence.claim: Folding/unfolding is a recognized framework whose period-set relationships are under investigation.

status_evidence.title: What we need to find out the periods of a periodic difference equation
status_evidence.snippet: Periodic orbits depend on the periodic orbits of gcd(p, k) nonautonomous p/gcd(p,k)-periodic difference equations.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results characterize how periodic orbits decompose under folding, but a full Per-set relationship is not stated as resolved.
